visual_action: A slideshow of screenshots of tweets from X (formerly Twitter) chronologically documenting the brief, unsuccessful bid by Steve Scalise for Speaker of the House in October 2023. The dates on the tweets are circled in red. The sequence shows the announcement of his run on Oct 4, his GOP nomination win on Oct 11, a tweet highlighting he lacks the necessary votes, reports of opposition on Oct 12, and finally his withdrawal from the race and a tweet memorializing his one-day 'speakership' on Oct 12.

on_screen_text.text: CBS News @CBSNews House Majority Whip Steve Scalise of Louisiana and fellow Republican Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio announced Wednesday that they will each run for speaker of the House.
Manu Raju @mkraju #Breaking: Scalise wins GOP nomination in secret-ballot election to be speaker, per Rep. Issa. Says the vote was 113-99

Do the Math –
Currently –
Hakeem Jeffries 212
Steve Scalise 113
Jim Jordan 99
House Speaker needs 217

Manu Raju @mkraju Lot of problems for Scalise. Just talked to Gimenez, Massie, Roy, Ogles, Max Miller. All are NO on Scalise. Massie says he’s a “hard no.” At least a dozen others are in same camp. He can only afford to lose four Rs.
Kyle Griffin @kylegriffin1 BREAKING: Steve Scalise is dropping out of the Speaker's race.
Aaron Rupar @atrupar RIP Steve Scalise's speakership (October 11, 2023-October 12, 2023)

spoken_summary: There is no speech or dialogue. The audio consists entirely of a sentimental song with a female vocalist and acoustic guitar. The lyrics include: "I always knew this day would come, we'd be standing one by one... I always knew after all these years, there'd be laughter, there'd be tears..."
audio_music: A slow, sentimental, and somewhat melancholic song plays throughout the video, featuring a female vocalist and an acoustic guitar. The style resembles a graduation or farewell song, which creates a mocking and ironic tone when juxtaposed with the political failure being documented.
editing_pacing: The video is a simple, slow-paced slideshow, with one screenshot of a tweet cutting to the next.
cultural_references: The hashtag '#GirlMath' is used, referencing an internet meme/trend that humorously justifies spending habits, here applied sarcastically to the vote count for Speaker of the House.
central_claim: Steve Scalise's bid for Speaker of the House was a swift and embarrassing failure due to Republican infighting and disarray.
intended_effect: To mock Steve Scalise and the Republican party, portraying them as chaotic and incapable of governing.
